\subsection{1. Quality audit of A2-Retry}




\subsubsection{1.1 Result quality}




The A2-Retry result is usable.




It collected \textbf{17 examples}, which satisfies the requested range of \textbf{12–20} examples. The sources include real public PDFs, personal resume pages, GitHub resume content, recruiter blind CVs, and sample resumes.




However, the source quality is mixed. The strongest examples are personal websites and public PDFs. The weakest examples are generic sample resumes and one disordered Scribd document.

\subsection{4. Benchmark patterns}




\subsubsection{4.1 Strong CVs use a narrow headline}




The strongest examples do not use broad titles like “creative developer” or “3D generalist” as the main positioning. They use direct role labels:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Technical Artist
Senior Technical Artist
Senior Unity Developer
XR Developer
Unity Expert
3D Visualization Artist
\end{mdcode}




Alexander should use a narrow headline, not a broad identity label.




Recommended primary headline:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
\end{mdcode}




Alternative headline for Unity-heavy applications:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity WebGL Developer focused on Technical Visualization
\end{mdcode}




Alternative headline for 3D/technical art applications:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity Technical Artist focused on CAD-to-Realtime Visualization
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{4.2 Strong CVs show proof before personality}




The best examples prioritize evidence:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
role → project → tools → responsibility → result
\end{mdcode}




Weak examples rely on generic traits:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
passionate
creative
hard-working
team player
problem solver
\end{mdcode}




Alexander’s CV should minimize soft claims and increase visible proof.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{4.3 Strong CVs expose project scale}




The best CVs include scale markers such as:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
5 shipped titles
40,000 downloads
150k+ downloads
500k users
100+ hours saved
2,500+ assets
33 ms frame-time budget
4 GB memory budget
\end{mdcode}




Alexander should not invent metrics. He should add measured or verifiable project metrics once the TwinSight evaluation is complete.




Usable current metrics from the thesis context:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
28 canonical research parts
30 scene nodes
257 technical elements
Unity WebGL target
30 FPS target = 33 ms frame-time budget
CAD-to-realtime pipeline
mobile-first interface
\end{mdcode}




Metrics still pending:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
actual FPS
actual frame time
load time
memory use
SUS score
NASA-TLX Raw score
participant count
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{4.4 Strong CVs organize technical skills by function}




The better examples group skills by category. They do not dump every tool into one long list.




Recommended skill grouping for Alexander:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-time development
3D production pipeline
Technical visualization
Web deployment
Automation and tooling
Version control
\end{mdcode}




Bad pattern to avoid:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity, Blender, Photoshop, Python, WebGL, Substance, Git, C#, AI, UX, UI, AR, VR, etc.
\end{mdcode}




That kind of list dilutes positioning.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{4.5 Strong CVs connect portfolio and resume}




The strongest examples include links to one or more of:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
portfolio
GitHub
project pages
PDF resume
LinkedIn
live demos
store pages
itch.io
\end{mdcode}




Alexander’s CV should link directly to:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
portfolio site
TwinSight live demo
TwinSight GitHub repository
TwinSight case study
LinkedIn
ArtStation or 3D portfolio
\end{mdcode}




The CV should not depend on the reader searching manually.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{5. Recommended CV structure for Alexander}




\subsubsection{5.1 Primary structure}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
1. Header
2. Role headline
3. 2–3 line professional summary
4. Core technical stack
5. Selected project: TwinSight X500
6. Additional projects
7. Technical skills
8. Education
9. Languages
10. Links
\end{mdcode}




\subsubsection{5.2 Why this structure}




Alexander has limited formal industry experience in Unity/Technical Art. Therefore, the CV should be \textbf{project-led}, not employment-led.




The CV should make TwinSight function as the main proof of capability.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsection{6. CV content recommendations}




\subsubsection{6.1 Header}

\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.2 Summary}




Recommended summary style:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
2–3 lines
specific role target
specific stack
specific proof project
no inflated seniority
\end{mdcode}




Draft baseline:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment. Built TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone through optimized 3D assets, technical UI, and mobile-first interaction design.
\end{mdcode}




For a one-page CV, this can be shortened to:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on Unity WebGL, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and interactive technical visualization. Creator of TwinSight X500, a web-based 3D drone assembly inspection prototype.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.3 Core technical stack}




Recommended stack block:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity | C# | WebGL | URP | UI Toolkit | Shader Graph
Blender | CAD-to-Realtime | UVs | Texture Baking | Optimization
Python | Git/GitHub | Technical Documentation | Usability Testing
\end{mdcode}




This is stronger than a long mixed list because it mirrors the job family.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.4 TwinSight X500 section}




Recommended section title:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Selected Technical Project — TwinSight X500
\end{mdcode}




Recommended role line:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Prototype | Thesis Project
\end{mdcode}




Recommended bullets:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
- Designed and developed a Unity WebGL prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone through interactive 3D visualization.
- Built a CAD-to-realtime pipeline using Blender, mesh cleanup, modular fasteners, UV preparation, texture baking, and Unity optimization.
- Structured the model into 28 canonical research parts, 30 scene nodes, and 257 technical elements for inspection and interaction.
- Designed a mobile-first interface with Unity UI Toolkit for part selection, isolation, transparency, and assembly understanding.
- Prepared technical evaluation around frame time, load time, memory use, usability, perceived workload, and qualitative feedback.
\end{mdcode}




Do not claim final performance metrics until measured.




When measured, add one bullet like:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
- Achieved [X] FPS / [Y] ms frame time / [Z] MB memory use in WebGL testing on [device/browser].
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.5 Additional project sections}




If the CV has space, add 1–2 more projects. These should reinforce the same positioning.




Useful project categories:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Blender technical asset study
Unity interaction prototype
Python automation/tooling script
real-time shader or visualization experiment
WebGL deployment experiment
\end{mdcode}




Avoid unrelated projects unless they prove technical art, Unity, or pipeline ability.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.6 Education wording}




Recommended wording:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
B.Eng. Multimedia Engineering — UNAD
Thesis: TwinSight X500, Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection
\end{mdcode}




If needed:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Former Electronic Engineering coursework — Universidad Nacional de Colombia
\end{mdcode}




The UNAL background should be secondary. It can support technical credibility, but it should not distract from the current target role.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\subsubsection{6.7 Languages}




Recommended wording:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Spanish — Native
English — C1 working proficiency
German — A1 / beginner
Portuguese — planned strategic learning
\end{mdcode}




For job applications, include only languages relevant to the role or region.




Do not overstate German or Portuguese.




\medskip\hrule\medskip

Execute A3_github_profiles_benchmark.

Collect public GitHub profile examples relevant to Alexander’s positioning:

- Badges/topics used
- Demo links
- Portfolio links
- License/disclaimer handling

- What Alexander can adapt
- What Alexander should not copy

- Date checked
